basis: Progressive skeletal myopathy; ptosis 24/24 and ophthalmoplegia 14/20 indicate ocular dysfunction. Dysphagia reflects affected swallowing muscles.
Inherited combined immunodeficiency directly impairs T- and B-lymphocyte function; infections and additional organ damage vary across subtypes.
Cerebellar and motor-neuron degeneration; hearing impairment 80-99% and skeletal muscle atrophy 9/14. Abnormal eye movements are neurologic signs.
Inherited retinal degeneration with night blindness, retinal pigmentation and optic disc pallor in 4/4.
Pituitary/CNS malformations define disease; spine defects and hearing loss 80-99%. Oral malformations and night blindness omitted at four-axis cap.
Leukemic blood-cell neoplasm infiltrating the testis; reproductive location adds no axis, and endocrine dysfunction is not established.
Severe neurodevelopmental impairment and epilepsy define disease; laryngomalacia causes structural airway dysfunction in 26/35.
Umbrella category of inborn mitochondrial transport defects; no additional organ damage is established across most subtypes.
Atonic-astatic neurologic syndrome characterized by hypotonia, ataxia and inability to stand or walk; no intrinsic muscle disease established.
Malignant smooth-muscle neoplasm arising in skin; the broad EBV-associated ancestor does not establish infection in this concept.
Brainstem and cerebellar hypoplasia with severe developmental impairment; neutropenia and thrombocytopenia each 2/9, below threshold.
Usually infectious inflammation of the pharyngeal tonsil in the upper respiratory tract.
Neurologic disorder with alternating hemiplegic episodes; no additional organ damage established across the umbrella.
Intrinsic dysfunction of phagocytic blood cells impairs chemotaxis and innate immunity; no specific additional organ damage established.
Vascular and skeletal connective-tissue disease; cleft palate and abnormal skin scarring each 30-79%. Asthma is a separate associated disease.
Renal tubular disease; syndromic seizures/ID, sensorineural hearing loss and chronic pancreatic injury each 2/5. Secondary hypertension excluded.
Progressive epilepsy; scoliosis 2/2 and generalized amyotrophy 1/2 support musculoskeletal involvement. Microglossia lacks documented functional damage.
B-cell lymphoma, usually localized to lymph nodes; splenic, hepatic and marrow abnormalities are occasional, below 30%.
Congenital pulmonary valve, ventricular septal and ductal abnormalities are all cardiovascular; pulmonary valve refers to the heart.
Ovarian trophoblastic/germ-cell malignancy has reproductive origin; hCG secretion alone does not establish an endocrine-organ disease.
Neurologic, phalangeal and nail defects define syndrome; optic atrophy 2/2. Ventricular septal defect 1/3 omitted at four-axis cap.
Fibrosarcoma arising in breast, an excluded organ; fibroblastic histology does not establish locomotor connective-tissue involvement.
Histoplasma infection directly inflames the meninges; additional systemic sites are not required or established as common for this concept.
Retinal dystrophy, obesity and polydactyly are defining features; developmental delay 12/12 and intellectual disability 13/19. Renal hypoplasia only 1/12.
Subcutaneous parasite causes blistering and skin ulceration; arthritis and restricted joint mobility are reported in 30-79%. GI symptoms lack organ damage.
